what: One address for any stored value, and the thin read-only class that reads it. The scheme names the root (cairn: the repo, cairncommons: the commons, instance: ~/.cairn, claude: ~/.claude, file: a real path); the path finds the record; # walks inside it (#KEY env, #section/key ini, #a/b/c json). `ref(address)` hands back a Dataref, or a Secret for a secret:<address>. A Dataref caches its file until the stat stamp (inode, size, mtime_ns) moves. A Secret's str, repr, format and .value are **********; .secret reads fresh and keeps nothing; it cannot be pickled or json-dumped. A miss raises DatarefMiss naming the address, never a value.
why: Akien, 2026-11-09, on CC0AC-Weather's file:secrets.env#KEY: 'it looks like the perfect way to do file pointers for everything', and 'a class. it's __str__ would return ********** but it's .secret would return the value fetched from the file.' Measured the same day: one .env line parse written three times (web_operator._env_value, ccfox env_value, CC0AC private.py), the Law 1 defect address.py was born to stop, and a secret held as a plain str prints wherever it is passed.
invoke: `from cairn.tools.dataref import ref, Dataref, Secret, DatarefMiss`; `ref('secret:instance:///devices/cc/0/.env#githubtoken').secret`. No CLI door. Prove: `python3 cairn/tools/dataref/proofs/test_dataref.py`.
entry: FRESH build, 2026-11-09, ticket 060d2146618c. Stands on cairn/tools/base/address.py (ROOTS, resolve) rather than a second root table. Prior art cited, not grafted: pydantic SecretStr (masked str), fsspec (one interface over many stores), jar:file: and view-source: (one-colon wrapping), RFC 6901 (a json path after #).
state_and_history: state.json + history.json beside this charter, born at the ticket's BUILDME crossing through harbor_master.clearance.clear.
how_it_learns: It does not; it is a pure reader. Its reads counter is the instrument the metric at outline 17.27 will count to test the cache HYPOTHESIS (17.28.4).
learns: It does not; it is a pure reader.
filed_edges: (a) db: and host addresses refuse as not built: db: waits for db_domain's client (17.28.3), a host for a bus read (17.28.1.2).
(b) A same-size, same-mtime_ns rewrite in place is not seen by the cache. Accepted: an atomic replace gets a new inode, and a Secret never caches.
(c) Masking covers str/repr/format/.value/pickle/json; it cannot stop a caller writing s.secret into a log. Every unmasking is a greppable .secret.
(d) ccfox and ccgoogle (~/.local/bin, outside git) still read CC's .env by hand; they are host tools, not yet users.
gates: proof gate — proofs/test_dataref.py, six teeth, one per falsifier clause of ticket 060d2146618c, over a scratch roots table. Durability gate: committed + pushed.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) a built scheme resolves to the wrong file, or cairn:/// / instance:/// differ from address.resolve's repo/ and instance/; (2) the # walk misreads env, ini or json; (3) any printing of a Secret shows its value, or pickle/json.dumps of one succeeds; (4) a changed file is not re-read, or an unchanged one is; or a Secret keeps its value; (5) a miss does not raise DatarefMiss naming the address, or its message or chain carries a value; (6) web_operator.secret reads anywhere but through a Secret. WRONG-SHAPE SIGNAL: a write method here, or a second root table.

feedback.why: a miss in the field is a care-of-the-code finding: an address someone wrote that no longer resolves.
